title: 2026 waste-battery air-emissions monitoring and limits QA controls

sources.title: Waste batteries: appropriate measures - emissions monitoring and limits
Waste batteries: appropriate measures for permitted facilities

facts.source_fact: Permit emission limits and monitoring requirements may be set from the emissions inventory and environmental risk assessment, and may be lower than guidance values where needed to protect the environment.
facts.expected_handling: Treat permit-specific limits as authoritative for the facility.

facts.source_fact: Facilities must create and maintain an inventory of point-source emissions to air and water, including sewer discharges.
The air-emissions inventory includes flow, temperature, concentration, load, variability, flammability, explosive limits, reactivity and substances affecting treatment or safety.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve measured characteristic and variability context.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring locations must meet MCERTS standards and monitoring must use MCERTS-qualified accredited methods and certified staff.
facts.expected_handling: Carry method and personnel certification evidence.

facts.source_fact: Emissions monitoring must be carried out when plant is operating at or near full treatment capacity, with processing rate and air-flow rate recorded and submitted.
facts.expected_handling: Attach operating-load context to monitoring results.

facts.source_fact: Dust monitoring uses EN 13284-1 every 6 months with a 5 mg/m3 emission limit unless the permit states alternative requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Store standard, frequency, unit and permit override together.

facts.source_fact: TVOC monitoring uses EN 12619 every 6 months with a 30 mg/m3 emission limit where relevant unless the permit states alternative requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Apply relevance and permit-override gates before comparison.

facts.source_fact: Total mercury monitoring uses EN 13211 every 3 months with a 7 microgram/m3 emission limit where applicable unless the permit states alternative requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve microgram units and monitoring frequency.

facts.source_fact: Hydrogen chloride is monitored every 6 months to EN 1911 with a 10 mg/m3 limit and hydrogen fluoride every 6 months to CEN TS 17340 with a 1 mg/m3 limit unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Keep pollutant, standard, frequency and limit paired correctly.

facts.source_fact: Periodic monitoring normally reports the average of 3 consecutive measurements of at least 30 minutes each; longer sampling may be required for some parameters and frequency may only be reduced where emissions are proven sufficiently stable.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve averaging period and evidence for any reduced frequency.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve cited standard, limit and scope.
Check facility permit before using guidance limit.
Attach guidance and permit version dates.
Bind result to the specified monitoring standard or approved alternative.
Bind result to required monitoring frequency and any approved reduction evidence.
Retain monitoring-location, method and staff certification context.
Do not convert facility stack results into parcel-level measurements.
Flag missing standard, unit, permit or operating-context evidence.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Silent acceptance of incomplete monitoring records.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; 10 x 10 = 100 controls
